_comment: ATS source registry for daily_screen.py. greenhouse/lever/ashby: slug -> display name. workday: 'host|tenant|site' -> name. Every entry verified live (HTTP 200) on 2026-09-16; dead slugs pruned, migrations re-homed. 422-Workday entries kept under _removed_workday_422 pending site-name discovery; non-API/defunct companies under _deferred. Re-verify the whole file with `python3 src/screening/daily_screen.py --validate`. Four Workday triples were recovered by careers-page harvesting (capitalone/Capital_One, workday/Workday, micron/External, paloaltonetworks/panwexternalcareers), and two by brute-forcing the site name (cisco/Cisco_Careers, salesforce/External_Career_Site). This registry is a starting point, not an exhaustive list: `src/screening/harvest_board_slugs.py` adds more, and a slug is only trusted once it has been verified live. This file lives in the DATA directory, not in `src/`, for the same reason the rest of the configuration does: the boards you track are yours, and a second person keeps their own. `queries` and `timezone` below were constants in `daily_screen.py`.

_deferred.note: Companies that have no clean JSON ATS API or a defunct careers site — need CDP/browser rendering or a new ATS to be added back.
_deferred.deel: jobs.deel.com is a Next.js SPA with no public JSON API; previous ashby board is empty. Re-add once an API or CDP scrape is confirmed.
_deferred.safety: safety.com/careers 301-redirects to gcd.com/protected/ (defunct/relocated); previous ashby board is empty.

_removed_workday_422.note: tenant exists but site name wrong (HTTP 422); needs careers-page discovery

_removed_hard_bar.greenhouse:spacex: Removed 2026-10-02: the whole board requires ITAR / U.S. Person status. Its JDs carry an explicit ITAR REQUIREMENTS section, so none of its jobs can ever be applied to by this candidate. It had 2648 postings, which flooded the fresh-candidate list - 201 of 204 zero-row candidates came from this one board - so keeping it in the registry hid the boards that might actually be usable.

filters_comment: WHAT MAKES A POSTING WORTH REPORTING, in the applicant's own words rather than in the code's. These values are the software-engineering defaults this tool shipped with - they describe ONE person's field and region (a backend software engineer looking at US postings), and they are wrong for anyone else - so a nurse, a lawyer or a designer replaces them. `field_include` is what your field is called in a TITLE and every posting has to match it, or it is counted as `not_engineering` and never reported; when this key is ABSENT the words are taken from `resume_tracks` -> `keywords` in candidate_profile.json instead, which is where you have already written what your field is. `region_include`/`region_exclude` are read from a posting's location field; `title_region_include`/`title_region_exclude` catch the region when it is written in the TITLE instead, which is how a board that leaves locations blank still screens. A LIST is the words themselves and each one matches a whole word, so `nurse` does not screen "Nursery School Teacher"; a STRING is a regex, for a field a word list cannot describe. `field_exclude` and `title_topics_exclude` are NEGATIVE preferences - the adjacent roles you do not want to read about - so leaving them out means you have none, and NOT that another person's are used. Naming a field and no region turns the region gate OFF rather than defaulting it: which region you can work in is yours to state, and a wrong one silently hides postings.
skip_title_comment: THE TITLES THAT ARE NOT WORTH READING - a third question from both `field_include` and `levels`. Those two ask is this my field, and which rung is it; this one asks is this a role family I have already decided not to read. TWO KINDS OF WORD LIVE HERE and only one of them is yours to write. THE GENERAL HALF - manager, director, lead, head, architect, intern, recruiter, account, analyst, sales, support, solutions - is how every field writes the manager/lead track and the families beside it, so no key is offered for it: both scanners apply those words wherever you point them, and `levels.management` is the same judgement spelled for a field that writes a management title with its own word ("Director of Nursing"). THE FIELD HALF IS THIS KEY, and the values above are software's: a `qa`, `ios`, `android`, `devops` or "data engineer" title says nothing about whether a hospital's board holds a role worth reading, and carrying the list onto one would drop clinical informatics roles nobody asked the tool to judge. Replace them with your own field's noise. The rule is the one the other negatives follow: these words stand while there is no `filters` block at all, and once you write one, a `skip_title` you do not name means NO skip gate rather than someone else's - a blocked title is a posting you never see, so the safe direction is to show one that could have been hidden. A LIST is the words themselves, each matching a whole word; a STRING is a regex.
levels_comment: WHICH RUNG A POSTING IS ON, which is a different question from `filters` and gets its own block because the words are different ones: "Senior" and "Staff" are not words for the work, they are words for how much of it someone has done, and they are spelled the same in every field. What is NOT the same in every field is the spelling a field gives its own rungs - software writes "Software Engineer II", "SWE II" and "IC2"; nursing writes "RN II"; law writes "Associate". These four values are the software spellings the screen shipped with, so they are what a registry that names no levels still reads; a nurse, a lawyer or a designer replaces the words in each one. `junior`, `mid` and `senior` decide the LEVEL the posting is ranked by (lower-seniority postings first), so a field's own rungs left unstated cost those postings their ranking weight and show up in the report as `level: unknown`. `management` is the one that REMOVES a posting: it is the manager/lead track the applicant does not want, not a rung, and a field's own management titles ("Director of Nursing", "Nurse Manager") are kept and ranked as ordinary roles until they are named here. A LIST is the words themselves, each matching a whole word; a STRING is a regex, as the four defaults are. `levels` is read by src/screening/daily_screen.py through src/screening/screen_newgrad_postings.py -> level_patterns.
timezone_comment: THE IANA ZONE THE DAILY REPORT IS FILED UNDER. It decides the date on the filename, so a run near midnight files under the wrong day if this is not where you are.
